_meta.description: WCP cross-SDK governance conformance test vectors. All SDKs that do NOT appear in skip_sdks for a given vector MUST produce the declared denied outcome and deny_code.

deny_code_notes.MISSING_CORRELATION_ID: Go uses this code without the DENY_ prefix. Equivalent to Python/TS DENY_MISSING_CORRELATION_ID.
deny_code_notes.NO_AVAILABLE_WORKER: Go uses this code without the DENY_ prefix. Equivalent to Python/TS DENY_NO_AVAILABLE_WORKER.
deny_code_notes.INVALID_BLAST_SCORE: Go uses this for blast_score range errors. Python does not validate blast_score range at make_decision() level. TS uses DENY_INVALID_INPUT.

parity_gaps: CV-003: CLOSED. Python now validates blast_score range in make_decision() step 0.25. All SDKs agree.
CV-004: CLOSED. Python now validates blast_score range in make_decision() step 0.25. All SDKs agree.

CV-007: Go uses per-worker RequiredControls checked at candidate selection (NO_AVAILABLE_WORKER). Python/TS use rule-level required_controls_suggested enforced at step 3 (DENY_MISSING_REQUIRED_CONTROLS).
CV-009/CV-010: Go enforces AllowedEnvironments per-worker in the registry. Python/TS enforce via rule match conditions — no per-worker env filter exists in those SDKs.
CV-012: Go rejects the input (INVALID_CAPABILITY_ID). Python/TS sanitize and route normally (no match since capability_id with newline wont match any rule).

vectors.description: No available worker for capability — no workers enrolled — must be denied
vectors.notes: Python/TS: no candidates in rule decision -> DENY_NO_AVAILABLE_WORKER. Go: empty registry -> NO_WORKER_FOR_CAPABILITY then deny. For cross-SDK parity: Python/TS use rule with empty candidate list; Go uses empty registry.

vectors.description: blast_score=-1 (below valid range) must be denied as invalid input
vectors.skip_reason: Parity gap closed: Python now validates blast_score range [0,100] in make_decision() step 0.25. All three SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go) correctly reject out-of-range blast_score values.

vectors.description: blast_score=101 (above valid range) must be denied as invalid input
vectors.skip_reason: Parity gap closed: Python now validates blast_score range [0,100] in make_decision() step 0.25. All three SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go) correctly reject out-of-range blast_score values.

vectors.description: blast_score=0 is the valid lower boundary — must be allowed (denied=false)
blast_score=100 in dev env — valid upper boundary below the deny-threshold — must be allowed
vectors.notes: In dev blast gate is not active by default (no hall floor for dev). blast_score=100 is a valid value and must not be rejected. The blast gate only denies >=85 in prod/edge.

vectors.description: Required control declared by rule but absent from registry — must be denied
vectors.notes: Python/TS: rule declares required_controls_suggested=[ctrl.obs.audit-log-append-only], registry has no such control -> DENY_MISSING_REQUIRED_CONTROLS. Go: worker declares RequiredControls=[ctrl.obs.audit-log-append-only] but no other worker provides it via CurrentlyImplements -> candidate skipped with required_controls_missing -> NO_AVAILABLE_WORKER. Both SDKs deny — different code path, same governance outcome.

vectors.description: Required control declared by rule and present in registry — must be allowed
vectors.notes: Python/TS: rule declares required_controls_suggested=[ctrl.obs.audit-log-append-only], registry has it -> allowed. Go: worker declares RequiredControls=[ctrl.obs.audit-log-append-only] and a second enrolled worker provides it via CurrentlyImplements -> allowed.

vectors.description: Worker with AllowedEnvironments=[dev] requested in prod — must be denied
vectors.skip_reason: Go enforces AllowedEnvironments per-worker in the registry at candidate selection. Python and TypeScript use JSON routing rules for environment filtering — no per-worker AllowedEnvironments concept exists in those SDKs. Env restriction in Python/TS is enforced by the rule match condition (env field), not post-selection. This vector tests Go-only behavior.

vectors.description: Worker with AllowedEnvironments=[dev] requested in dev — must be allowed
Valid request — all checks pass — must be allowed (denied=false)
capability_id with embedded newline (control character) — telemetry sanitization invariant: no control chars in capability_id field in any emitted telemetry
vectors.skip_reason: Go rejects the request at validateRouteInput (INVALID_CAPABILITY_ID, denied=true) before any telemetry is emitted with the mangled capability_id. The invariant test (no control chars in telemetry) is vacuously satisfied on Go's deny path because the capability_id is sanitized in buildDenyTelemetry via SanitizeID. This vector focuses on the Python/TS sanitization path where the request MAY be routed.
vectors.notes: Python and TypeScript: neither rejects capability_id containing a newline at the routing layer (Python's RouteInput and TS's validateRouteInput only check for null/empty, not control chars in capability_id). The wildcard rule matches, routing proceeds. Both SDKs sanitize the capability_id in telemetry output via their _CTRL_CHARS_RE / sanitizeID logic. The shared invariant: telemetry must not contain the raw newline. Go covers the deny path separately in router_test.go (TestCapabilityIDWithNewlineIsRejected).

vectors.description: Worker attestation: enroll with hash, verify match, mutate file, verify DENY_WORKER_TAMPERED
vectors.skip_reason: CV-013 is a multi-step procedural test requiring file I/O — implemented as standalone test in each SDK test suite, not driven by the conformance vector loader
steps: Enroll worker with attestation registered (SHA-256 of source file)
Mutate the worker source file (change one byte)
Verify evidence receipt includes worker_attestation_checked=true, worker_attestation_valid=false
vectors.note: Hash values (registered_hash, current_hash) are NOT in the deny payload — F4 security requirement prohibits leaking hash values to callers.
